name: Sadler Chapel United Methodist Church
researchNote:
FULL standard applied 2026-08-05 (site + church socials + pastor searched against all six markers). LEFT AT unknown. A BAD ROW IN THE SOURCE, and the denomination is the proof: this is SADLER CHAPEL UNITED METHODIST CHURCH, 15025 County Rd 468, Dexter MO 63841, pastored by Dave Fowler. The UMC ordains women and is the least likely denominational home in America for a postmillennial theonomic congregation; womens_ordination flag applied as a fact about the body. Its public activity as reported locally is hosting MONTHLY BLUEGRASS JAM SESSIONS, free and open to the public on the third Thursday — community music, which is a real ministry and is not any of the six markers. NEGATIVE RESULTS RECORDED: nothing on abortion, postmillennialism, theonomy, Christian nationalism, Zionism or patriarchy. This is the fifth row in the cohort whose theological profile is flatly inconsistent with its listing.

=== MISSOURI PASTOR'S PETITION, cross-referenced 2026-08-05 ===
SIGNED BY: Pastor Joe Myers. MISSOURI PASTOR'S PETITION (Abolish Abortion Missouri, abolishabortionmo.org/pastors-petition), captured 2026-08-05. Signed by pastors, elders and deacons; its stated ground is that "Since the overturning of Roe v. Wade unborn babies are still not equally protected under Missouri law, as born persons are." That is the equal-protection claim, and signing it is a first-hand, formal, attributable act by a named man at a named church — the same class of evidence as the Iowa, Nebraska and Ohio equal-protection statements. Abolish Abortion Missouri is named in the Norman Statement through Wes Scroggins and Kevan Myers. AND THIS CORRECTS A DISMISSAL I MADE EARLIER THE SAME DAY. Researching the postmillennial-directory cohort, I read this row as "a bad row in the source" — United Methodist, a denomination that ordains women, whose only visible public activity was hosting monthly bluegrass jam sessions — and recorded "nothing on abortion, postmillennialism, theonomy, Christian nationalism, Zionism or patriarchy." A pastor of this church had signed the Missouri equal-protection petition. I dismissed it on DENOMINATIONAL grounds, which is the rule "denominational inference is not research" being broken in the negative direction — the harder direction to catch, because a wrong dismissal leaves no trace. LEADERSHIP NOTE: the petition lists JOE MYERS; local press gave DAVE FOWLER. Both are recorded; neither is discarded, and which is current is unresolved. THE CONGREGATION HAS NOT BEEN READ ON ITS OWN TERMS: denomination, eschatology and the remaining five markers are unset, and culturalEngagement is single_issue because a signature evidences one public question and nothing about breadth. That is what signature_only records.

**DEMOTED FROM QUALIFYING 2026-08-05 — consistency pass, not a new judgement.**

This church was marked transformationalist on 2026-07-30 because **postmillennialworldview.com** lists its pastor as postmillennial, under the standard then in force: one of the six markers was enough, and a third-party listing counted as church-level corroboration.

**That standard was replaced on 2026-07-31.** Transformationalist now requires **evidenced corporate civil-sphere engagement**. On that rule 123 churches whose pastors had personally signed public equal-protection statements were demoted — and **a signature is a first-hand, attributable act, while a listing on someone else's website is not**. Leaving this cohort qualifying while demoting those would have been incoherent.

It also fails on a second count. **Postmillennialism is an eschatology, not an action.** Even fully verified it would establish what a church expects God to do in history, not that the congregation acts corporately on public questions — which is what this directory classifies on.

**Nothing has been deleted.** The postmillennial attribution stays on the record above as a **research lead**, and the row keeps its `verify_stance` flag. Read the church's own site, socials and preaching, and if it acts corporately on public questions it should be promoted back on that evidence — and would then rank on however many of the six markers it actually meets.

**One caution on the source:** an earlier check of eight pastor attributions from this same directory found **seven stale or wrong**, so the postmillennial claim itself needs verifying before it is relied on.
